title: Harvesting mouse suprachiasmatic nucleus by vibrating microtome for diurnal transcriptome analysis
author: Bafna, Lau, et al.
materials: NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA Library Prep Kit
Mouse: C57Bl/6J background (8- 12 weeks-old) male or female
Dissection tools (forceps, needles, razor blades, small scissors, big scissors, brush)

The harvested SCN tissues are used for total RNA extraction to conduct polyA library preparation and sequencing. To increase the yield, SCN tissues collected at a single time-point are pooled prior to performing RNA extraction and purification. Post quality assessment, the extracted RNA is subjected to polyA library preparation and sequencing on Illumina platform.20.Thaw the SCN tissues containing 1.5 mL tubes on ice for RNA extraction. Pool 3 individual SCN tissue samples suspended in Buffer RLT, collected at the same ZT in one separate RNAse free tube. This is referred as one biological replicate (BR) and labeled (for example; ZT2_BR1).CRITICAL: The tissue samples should be thawed completely on ice before transferring to another tube. Special care should be taken while pooling the samples to avoid cross-contamination.21.Adjust the sample volume to 350 μl with Buffer RLT and follow steps for RNA extraction using an RNeasy micro kit (Qiagen) as per the manufacturer’s instructions (https://www.qiagen.com/us/products/discovery-and-translational-research/dna-rna-purification/rna-purification/total-rna/rneasy-kits) for purification of total RNA from microdissected cryosections using laser microdissection systems. The extracted RNA is finally eluted in 14 μl elution buffer supplied with the kit. During the RNA extraction, perform on-column DNase digestion as per manufacturer’s guidelines.Note: Alternatively, if the brain tissue of interest is different (such as cortex, striatum etc.) any suitable commercial RNA extraction kit such as RNAqueous Kit (https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/AM1912), PureLink RNA Mini kit (https://www.thermofisher.com/uk/en/home/life-science/dna-rna-purification-analysis/rna-extraction/rna-types/total-rna-extraction/purelink-rna-mini-kit.html) or TRIzol based RNA purification method7 can be adopted for RNA extraction.Pause point: The extracted RNA can be stored for long term at −80°C.22.Inspect the quality and quantity of the extracted RNA for each sample on Bioanalyzer using Agilent RNA 6000 pico chip. For library preparation, do not include any RNA sample with RIN (RNA integrity number) < 7.0 (Figure 6). See ‘troubleshooting’ for more details.Figure 6RNA quality assessment using BioanalyzerExample of bioanalyzer report for quality assessment of the extracted RNA samples (lane numbered 1–11) along with the ladder (left, L). The two bands denote 28S (top) and 18S (bottom) rRNA.Note: Alternatively, RNA gel electrophoresis can be used to check for the integrity of the RNA, and Nanodrop to assess the purity and the concentration of the extracted RNA. Ideally, 260/280 ratio of ∼2.0 from Nanodrop is accepted as “pure” for RNA.23.Prepare libraries for sequencing, in accordance with the manufacturer’s guidelines for a NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA Library Prep Kit (https://uk.neb.com/products/e7760-nebnext-ultra-ii-directional-rna-library-prep-kit-for-illumina#Product%20Information) and subsequently sequence the polyA enriched libraries on Illumina based platform (single or paired end).

steps.title: Optional circadian behavior analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze wheel‑running activity of entrained mice for the last 7–10 days using ClockLab Analysis 6 (or any equivalent activity‑monitoring system) at a 24 h period; inspect rhythms with consistent settings (e.g., percentile/normalized actogram) and discard any animal that does not show robust rhythmic activity (ZT12‑ZT24).

substeps.instruction: Collect locomotor data for 7–10 days.
Open data in ClockLab (or equivalent) and inspect the 24 h rhythm using consistent analysis settings.
Exclude animals lacking robust rhythmicity from further study.

steps.title: Thaw and pool SCN tissues
steps.instruction: Place 1.5 mL tubes containing harvested SCN tissue on ice until completely thawed, then pool three individual SCN samples (all suspended in Buffer RLT and collected at the same ZT) into a single RNase‑free tube; label the pool as one biological replicate (e.g., ZT2_BR1) while avoiding cross‑contamination.

substeps.instruction: Thaw tubes on ice until fully liquid.
Transfer three Buffer RLT‑suspended SCN samples to one RNase‑free tube.
Label the pool (e.g., ZT2_BR1) and keep on ice.

steps.title: Adjust volume and extract RNA
steps.instruction: Bring the pooled sample volume to 350 µL with Buffer RLT, then extract total RNA using the Qiagen RNeasy Micro Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol for microdissected cryosections, performing on‑column DNase digestion; elute the purified RNA in 14 µL elution buffer. Alternative kits (RNAqueous, PureLink, TRIzol) may be used if desired.

substeps.instruction: Add Buffer RLT to reach 350 µL total volume.
Follow the RNeasy Micro Kit protocol, including on‑column DNase treatment.
Elute RNA in 14 µL supplied elution buffer.

steps.title: Store RNA and assess quality
steps.instruction: Store extracted RNA at –80 °C for long‑term preservation if needed. Assess RNA integrity on an Agilent Bioanalyzer using the RNA 6000 pico chip; only samples with RIN ≥ 7.0 proceed. Optionally verify integrity by gel electrophoresis and purity by NanoDrop (260/280 ≈ 2.0).

substeps.instruction: Freeze RNA at –80 °C (pause point).
Run Bioanalyzer RNA 6000 pico chip and record RIN.
If desired, run a denaturing gel and measure 260/280 ratio on NanoDrop.

steps.title: Prepare libraries and sequence
steps.instruction: Construct poly‑A‑enriched libraries using the NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA Library Prep Kit (product E7760) following the manufacturer’s instructions, then sequence the libraries on an Illumina platform (single‑ or paired‑end reads).

substeps.instruction: Perform library preparation with NEBNext Ultra II Directional kit.
Load libraries onto Illumina sequencer and run (single or paired end).

steps.title: Quality control of FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Run FastQC on each paired‑end FASTQ file (accept only reads with Phred quality ≥ 20) and trim Illumina adapters using TrimGalore v0.4.3.

substeps.instruction: Execute FastQC; discard reads with Phred < 20.
Trim adapters with TrimGalore version 0.4.3.

steps.title: Align reads and count genes
steps.instruction: Align the cleaned reads to the mouse mm10 genome using STAR v2.7.8a with MAPQ = 60 for unique mappers; generate gene‑level read counts with FeatureCounts via Samtools v1.11. As an alternative, upload FASTQ files to BioJupies to obtain raw count matrices.

substeps.instruction: Align with STAR v2.7.8a (MAPQ = 60).
Create BAM files and count reads per gene using FeatureCounts through Samtools v1.11.
Optional: use BioJupies web app to obtain count data.

steps.title: Detect rhythmic transcripts with dryR
steps.instruction: Prepare a data‑matrix file from the raw counts containing four biological replicates for each time‑point (ZT2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22). In R (installed from r‑project.org) run the dryR package (Differential RhythmicitY analysis in R): use plot_single_cond() for single‑condition rhythmicity or dryseq() to compare conditions. The analysis outputs a .csv file listing amplitude, phase, intercept, sine and cosine coefficients, p‑value and adjusted p‑value for each gene.

substeps.instruction: Create matrix with counts for ZT2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22 (four replicates each).
Load dryR in R and run plot_single_cond() or dryseq() as appropriate.
Export results to a .csv file containing amp, phase, intercept, s1, c1, pvalue, padj.

steps.title: Optional differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: If desired, perform differential expression with limma‑voom (Bioconductor limma v3.48.0) to obtain normalized log‑CPM values, then feed these values into rhythmicity detection tools such as ECHO or JTK_CYCLE.

substeps.instruction: Run limma‑voom on the count matrix to get log‑CPM.
Use ECHO, JTK_CYCLE, or similar methods on the normalized data.
